## Grade 9 EQAO Academic Math Box-Plots by Year

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# filter data by year
df1718 <- a2data %>%
  filter(year == "2017-2018")

ggplot(df1718, aes(
    x = reorder(board_type, percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_academic_mathematics, FUN = median, na.rm = TRUE), 
    y = percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_academic_mathematics, 
    fill = board_type # Automatically groups boxes side-by-side by school type
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "skyblue", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "grey")) + # Customize colours per type
  labs(
    title = "2017-2018 Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in academic mathematics in Catholic Schools across Ontario",
    x = "Schools in Ontario by Board Type",
    y = "Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in academic mathematics",
    fill = "School Type" # Legend title
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
summary(df1718$percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_academic_mathematics)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Start with the data frame (a2data %>%), then filter for 2024-2025
df2425 <- a2data %>%
  filter(trimws(as.character(year)) == "2024-2025") %>%
  mutate(
    board_type = trimws(as.character(board_type)),
    # Use the non-academic Grade 9 math column for 2024-2025
    score = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", as.character(percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_mathematics))))
  ) %>%
  # Rescale to 0-100 if stored as decimals
  mutate(
    score = if (!all(is.na(score)) && max(score, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1) score * 100 else score
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(score)) %>%
  mutate(board_type = factor(board_type, levels = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)")))

# 2. Check summary for Public schools ONLY in 2024-2025
summary(df2425$score[df2425$board_type == "Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)"])

# 3. Create the box plot (no reorder() so Public stays on top, no limits() in scale_y_continuous)
ggplot(df2425, aes(
    x = board_type,
    y = score,
    fill = board_type
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "skyblue", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "grey"),
    breaks = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2024-2025 Percentage of Grade 9 Students Achieving Provincial Standard in Mathematics",
    x = "Schools in Ontario by Board Type",
    y = "Percentage of Grade 9 Students Achieving Provincial Standard (%)",
    fill = "School Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

summary(df2425$percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_academic_mathematics)
```
Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

## Grade 9 EQAO Applied Math Box-Plots by Year
```{r, echo=FALSE}
df1718 <- a2data %>%
  filter(year == "2017-2018")

ggplot(df1718, aes(
    x = reorder(board_type, percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics, FUN = median, na.rm = TRUE), 
    y = percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics, 
    fill = board_type # Automatically groups boxes side-by-side by school type
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "lightpink", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "grey")) + # Customize colours per type
  labs(
    title = "2017-2018 Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in applied mathematics in Schools across Ontario",
    x = "Schools in Ontario by Board Type",
    y = "Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in applied mathematics",
    fill = "School Type" # Legend title
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
summary(df1718$percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
df1819 <- a2data %>%
  filter(year == "2018-2019",
    !is.na(percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics = as.numeric(gsub("%", "", as.character(percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics))),
    # Lock the exact order here (because coord_flip() reverses the axis, the LAST item listed goes on TOP)
    board_type = factor(board_type, levels = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)"))
  )

ggplot(df1819, aes(
    x = board_type, 
    y = percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics, 
    fill = board_type # Automatically groups boxes side-by-side by school type
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "lightpink", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)" = "grey")) + # Customize colours per type
  labs(
    title = "2018-2019 Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in applied mathematics in Schools across Ontario",
    x = "Schools in Ontario by Board Type",
    y = "Percentage of Grade 9 students achieving provincial standard in applied mathematics",
    fill = "School Type" # Legend title
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
summary(df1819$percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_applied_mathematics)
```
